subject: PO acceptance locks, invoice cadence options, and pricing buckets
messages:
From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@aurorahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber
Cc: Michael Park <michael.park@aurorahealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Procurement constraints for Redwood pilot (PO / invoice cadence / net terms)

Hi Jonas,

Following our vendor intake call this morning: procurement has three gating items before we can set up a supplier profile in our ERP. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate the following?

1) PO acceptance: we need the ability to reference our PO number on every invoice and have the PO included in the invoice header (not the body).
2) Invoice cadence: Aurora prefers consolidated monthly invoices per cost center, rather than weekly/biweekly statements. Is that possible for the pilot?
3) Net terms: default is Net45 for new vendors; procurement is open to Net30 for ARR commitments >= $75k/yr but needs that reflected in the SOW/contract.
4) Remittance instructions and AP contact must match the PO.

We can share a template PO and sample GL mapping. Attaching our PO template for clarity.

Can you loop in billing and confirm whether any discounts/packaging changes are required to meet a monthly cadence?

Thanks,
Laura Jensen
Director, Strategic Procurement
Aurora Health Systems

Attachment: Aurora_PO_Template.pdf

From: jonas_weber
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, ben_carter
Date: 2026-08-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement constraints for Redwood pilot (PO / invoice cadence / net terms)

Laura — thanks for the clear list and the template. Quick summary from our side:

- PO header: yes, we can surface the PO number in the invoice header and a PO metadata field so it maps to your ERP. We'll need the exact field name/value expectations (e.g., PO#, PO-Ref) — I can map those once you confirm the JSON key/sample.
- Monthly consolidated invoices: technically feasible. Our default billing pipeline emits weekly tokenized usage files; we can aggregate to monthly per cost center but that will change invoice timing and (minor) cashflow for Redwood.
- Net terms: Net30 for ARR >= $75k/yr is a product-sales negotiation. From a billing perspective, we can flag the account as Net30 when finance signs off on the commitment.

I'm looping in Vanessa and Ben to confirm the pricing/discount implications and whether we need to change packaging or create a dedicated billing SKU for monthly consolidation.

Next steps I propose:
- Vanessa: confirm whether packaging/pricing buckets require modification for monthly invoices and what discount bands (if any) you'd offer for monthly vs weekly billing.
- Ben: confirm whether finance can provision Net30 once the ARR threshold is met and outline the approval lead time.

I'll draft a mutual action plan and send a redlineable contract fragment with the PO/header fields included.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz
To: jonas_weber
Cc: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@aurorahealth.com>, ben_carter, grace_oconnor
Date: 2026-08-07T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement constraints for Redwood pilot (PO / invoice cadence / net terms)

Jonas / Laura — tagging in short pricing notes.

1) Packaging / Billing SKU approach: We typically map usage to billing SKUs that align with product buckets (inference tokens, embeddings, dedicated capacity). Consolidating to monthly invoices doesn't require new SKUs, but it does change how discounts are evaluated: our systems evaluate discount eligibility per invoice run. If Aurora moves to monthly aggregated invoicing, discounts tied to per-invoice volume (e.g., slabed volume discounts) will be evaluated monthly instead of weekly, which generally increases the likelihood of hitting higher slabs and therefore increases the effective discount to the buyer.
2) Discount cadence options: We can offer two patterns: a) keep existing slab thresholds and let the monthly aggregation naturally move Aurora into higher slabs (no changes needed), or b) create a commitment-based bucket that gives a guaranteed floor discount (e.g., 5% floor at $75k ARR). Option (b) needs legal + finance coordination and a short commitment clause.
3) Operational lift: monthly consolidation is operationally simple on our side, but we'll need to ship a mapping file (invoice -> cost center) in the MIP format you use.

Attached a working pricing buckets sheet and a short note on expected delta to Redwood revenue at sample usage profiles. Ben, any objections on offering a 5% commitment floor for the pilot if Aurora signs a 12-month commitment >= $75k?

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise GTM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_pricing_buckets.xlsx

From: ben_carter
To: jonas_weber, vanessa_ortiz
Cc: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@aurorahealth.com>, grace_oconnor
Date: 2026-08-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement constraints for Redwood pilot (PO / invoice cadence / net terms)

Short finance take: we can support Net30 for accounts that meet the ARR threshold and pass our credit checks. Approval timeline: 5–7 business days after receipt of signed commitment (finance + credit ops). A couple of notes:

- If Aurora requests Net30 earlier (during pilot) we can do a short-term credit hold and revisit at the formal commitment, but that requires an AP contact and a trade credit form (I can share).
- Offering a 5% floor discount tied to a 12-month $75k ARR commitment is acceptable for commercial to approve for a pilot; we'll mark the deal with an exception code for the first invoice cycle.
- Regarding invoice aggregation: please confirm whether Aurora wants a single consolidated monthly invoice per legal entity or per cost center — the per-cost-center ask has a modest engineering/ops lift but is doable.

I can prepare the finance checklist and the credit form if Aurora wants Net30 pre-commitment. Grace: once Aurora confirms cost center vs legal entity we can lock accounting setup.

— Ben Carter
Director, Finance Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@aurorahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber, vanessa_ortiz, ben_carter, grace_oconnor
Cc: Michael Park <michael.park@aurorahealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement constraints for Redwood pilot (PO / invoice cadence / net terms)

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what procurement needs. A few clarifications and asks before we proceed to contract:

1) We will require consolidated monthly invoices per cost center (one invoice per cost center per month). That is non-negotiable for Aurora's internal chargebacks.
2) We will commit to a 12-month pilot at $80k ARR if Redwood will provide: a) guaranteed Net30 from day one of the paying contract, and b) a 5% minimum discount floor documented in the SOW.
3) Procurement also needs the PO header field labelled exactly "Aurora_PO" with the PO number present in the header and a corresponding mapping key in any file we receive.

Please confirm you can:
- produce monthly consolidated invoices per cost center,
- include Aurora_PO as an invoice header field, and
- provide the Net30 + 5% floor in the draft SOW.

If confirmed, we'll circulate a signed commitment and send the signed PO immediately. Also attaching our internal AP remittance notes separately (will forward).

Best,
Laura Jensen
Director, Strategic Procurement
Aurora Health Systems

Attachment: AP_Remittance_Instructions.pdf
